spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Kephalaia Chapter: The Five Degrees of Divine Order and the Subjugation of Falsity from Evil

---

**¶1:** [GAP-1] Falsity from evil was overcome and subjugated by five complete degrees of divine order proceeding from the Divine itself.

**¶2:** The first degree is the Divine Love itself, which exists in infinite peace and incomprehensibility; as it is established in its own celestial ground, in its very being and essence.

**¶3:** Four degrees of divine proceeding were made manifest and came forth from the Divine Love itself. They were arranged into ten orders of completeness, and established in a fullness of twelve — all things of faith and charity in their total complex.

**¶4:** The second degree poured forth and was made manifest. It was revealed from the first degree of the Divine itself. It is the proceeding divine truth that gives spiritual birth, the Divine Proceeding, together with the Divine Truth in its first form sent forth into combat against evil and the complete array of truths belonging to it; these constitute the second degree of divine order.

**¶5:** The third degree is the Divine Wisdom that delights in truths, the Divine Providence that orders all things, the Divine Truth active in judgment and separation, together with the five modes of ordering that proceed from it. These constitute the third degree of divine order.

**¶6:** The fourth degree is the Divine Truth sent forth to redeem what is captive, together with the sustaining truth that elevates all things toward the Divine, and all the derivative truths and goods that were revealed from it. These constitute the fourth degree.

**¶7:** The fifth degree that came from the Divine Love is the Divine Wisdom made fully manifest, together with all the spiritual capacities it summoned forth, its emanations which were [GAP-2] brought into distinct existence. They poured forth and were made manifest from it.

**¶8:** This is how they were distributed and [GAP-3] arranged in complete orders: these five [GAP-4: REVIEW — truths belonging to] the Divine Truth in its first combat [GAP-5] constitute the entire spiritual structure; another five are the five modes of ordering belonging to the Divine Truth active in judgment, which are distributed to five distinct states, sustaining [GAP-6] the whole of spiritual order.

**¶9:** [GAP-7] In their fullness they form twelve orders of completeness, which [GAP-8 — comprise all things of faith and charity. There are] another two principles added to them: the calling of divine truth and the reception of it in good. These are the generative principle of good and the receptive principle of truth, which the Divine Wisdom by its full manifestation has appointed as continuations of its own operation [GAP-9] within the ground of the church and the [GAP-10] life within them.

**¶10:** [GAP-11: The descent] of the Divine Truth in its first form, which came forth [GAP-12] belonging to [GAP-13] a state of spiritual governance [GAP-14] held in high regard before those who belong to its own household of charity [GAP-15] — yet its enemies, the evils and falsities, [GAP-16] assaulted it and inflicted suffering by their wickedness; and they strip from it [GAP-17] its truths and its spiritual abundance; and they imprison [GAP-18: REVIEW — the divine truth in] captivity and seize from it its ordered companies. Yet it [GAP-19] prevails by its own self-emptying humility; and it takes courage and restrains its adversary [GAP-20] in patient silence.

**¶11:** Just as it is with such a person — a noble interior truth surrounded and beset on all sides by its adversaries — so also is the descent of the Divine Truth into its first combat, [GAP-21] against the dominant falsities, the enemies of wisdom.

**¶12:** In contrast, the coming of the Divine Truth in its judicial and ordering capacity, and the commission it received from the Divine Love, whereby it came upon all the dominant falsities — this differs from the descent of truth into its first combat. Its coming [GAP-22] follows upon and completes what the first combat began.

**¶13:** The coming of the Divine Truth as judge is thus: when it was sent from the Divine to elevate and rescue the truth that had been immersed in combat with evil. It is like the power of discernment that the governing love sends forth to overturn the violence done to that interior truth — the noble perception against which falsities from evil had sinned. And this discerning truth [GAP-23] is severe and unyielding [GAP-24] and it provides the means [GAP-25] by its righteousness and its power; and it also judges all who stand condemned according to their rebellious will, and renders to each according to what it deserves. Those falsities deserving correction it strikes with truths that compel. Again, those falsities deserving the removal of their faculties — indeed their [GAP-26] very capacity to act — it renders to them accordingly. [GAP-27] And it binds and restrains them by the bonds of divine order, and suspends them by [GAP-28] inversion of their own state, and thus it does to them by a righteous judgment. And it destroys them utterly, stripping their outermost covering of apparent truth [GAP-29] so that they are destroyed by a spiritual death [GAP-30] until they cease entirely. Again, [GAP-31: REVIEW — those falsities for] whom it is fitting [GAP-32] to be expelled from the states they have usurped — this it does according to righteous judgment; just as they had transgressed and sinned against the noble interior truth.

**¶14:** Also, the derivative truths serving the function of judgment, those who act in concert with the discerning truth — those belonging to it in great spiritual power — in an instant and with immediacy they carry out the purpose of their governing principle.

**¶15:** Now, just as this power of true discernment was sent from the governing love to overturn the violence done to the noble interior truth: so also is it with the Divine Truth active in judgment. It too was sent from the Sovereign of all wisdom to overturn the assault and violence against the truth that first descended into combat, against which the ruling principle of all falsity from evil had sinned. That ruling evil transgressed against it, together with all its rebellious derivative falsities. Therefore, when the Divine Truth in its judicial power came, it elevated and rescued the truth that had been immersed in combat.

**¶16:** Also, all the dominant falsities, the powers of evil that had transgressed against the truths belonging to the first divine combat — it has judged them by a righteous separation. It has bound them in both internal and external states. It placed each one in the condition fitting for its nature; it weighed each of them according to its cruelty and its tyranny. Some of them it enclosed entirely in restraint; others it inverted, depriving them of intelligence. Some [GAP-33] are utterly deprived of power; others are rendered quiescent for all time. Some among them are fixed beneath their associates, restricted by strong bonds of divine order; others it made dominant over their companions below, so that they may exercise their nature among those beneath them.

**¶17:** [GAP-34] When the Divine Love through its truth established the orderings of judgment [GAP-35] it was revealed to all the powers of falsity from evil. It judged them as a true discernment of what is good and what is evil [GAP-36]. This is the primary separation and ordering that the Divine Truth in its judicial power gave to the dominant falsities [GAP-37: REVIEW — on account of] the Divine Truth that first descended into combat. Indeed, it gave victory to that truth in proportion to its victory; but it condemned the ruling principle of all falsity from evil in proportion to that by which it had departed from order.

**¶18:** [GAP-38] This bond of restraint, of this nature, became [GAP-39] the fixed order of the external church until the final state when the natural form of the church will be dissolved; and it perishes in the ultimate love of the Divine and is separated. While wisdom returns to its divine origin, falsity from evil remains in restraint and bondage forever.

**¶19:** The coming also of the Divine Truth sent forth to redeem — when it came to inspect those goods and truths held captive in the natural and external degree: it is like a sovereign love that comes and surveys those who form truths into uses [GAP-40] and [GAP-41] and [GAP-42].

**¶20:** Also, those who are good among such formers of truth — the builders of spiritual understanding and the workers of genuine use whom it has placed in each state — it shall see that they have labored well and have devoted themselves to the works of the Divine according to their capacity. It shall rejoice with the Divine delight [GAP-43]. It shall acknowledge the workers of use who have constructed its spiritual forms [GAP-44: REVIEW — and fulfilled] its purposes.

**¶21:** Now, just as this sovereign love comes and surveys its spiritual structures and protections of truth, so also is the coming of the Divine Truth sent forth to redeem. For when it too came, it saw [GAP-45: REVIEW — the spiritual structures] established and prepared and [GAP-46] the orderings of all states arranged and set in their places, above and below, externally and internally, in the great pattern of divine design that its prior emanations had made. They had entered the combat before it — those who had established and formed the entire order of the church before it came. It saw the celestial and spiritual intelligences established and governing the protections of truth [GAP-47] guarding the entire governance of divine order [GAP-48] which the primary emanations of the Divine had accomplished. These are the Divine Truth in its first combat, and the Divine Truth active in judgment, and the Divine Proceeding — the truth that gives spiritual birth.

**¶22:** Therefore, when it saw them, that they had ordered all things with great wisdom, [GAP-49] as they were beheld it liberated [GAP-50] — in its coming, by which it arrived, it was made fully manifest to them. It says to the Divine Truth active in judgment: "The ordering that you have [GAP-51] established is good; what you decreed [GAP-52] you gave to them correspondingly — so that the falsities from evil were displaced and removed from the states of which they were not worthy."

---

**¶26:** Then the calling of divine truth and the reception of it in good — the great providence that came to the mixed states of good and evil in the natural person, which are set in conjunction — it permeated them, it was established in imperceptible silence. It sustains [GAP-53] throughout the entire process of regeneration until the final state when it can arise and stand firm in the ultimate love of the Divine. It will gather to itself all genuine good and truth, and form them into the completed spiritual person. You will also find that it purges and casts out from itself all the falsity and evil that are foreign to it. However, the good and the wisdom that are dispersed throughout all states — these it gathers into itself and builds upon the whole form of the regenerated person.

**¶27:** The time when this completed spiritual person shall be perfected in all its faculties and powers, then it can become free and ascend from that great combat of temptation through the Divine Truth that orders all things — its father — the one who comes and brings a [GAP-54] restored faculty. He brings it up from within the gathering of all things, the final dissolution and consuming of all that is merely natural.

**¶28:** Now, this providence — that calling and reception — resembles thus: celestial good in its settled form. If a person will take it and place it in natural truth in its active and unsettled state, it dissolves and permeates throughout that natural truth. It works in a further state in silence and imperceptible quiet, into the very interior [GAP-55] — yet also, the essential power and quality of this natural truth [GAP-56] is drawn toward the celestial good, and the natural truth yields its life and becomes still [GAP-57] in [GAP-58] and the [GAP-59] — the merely natural and external of this truth it shall purify and discard. However, the celestial good, the spiritual good, and the delight of truth — these it shall gather into itself.

**¶29:** Again, this too is what the coming of that interior perception is like — the providence of spiritual life, which is the calling of divine truth and its reception in good — that came to the mixed natural states. This is the one that at the final state of regeneration can arise and stand firm, and will gather into itself all the goods and all the wisdom that has remained dispersed throughout every state. It can build them upon the whole form of its spiritual body; it will gather them into itself [GAP-60] in the likeness of the Divine forever and ever [GAP-61] from this time onward.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [Concerning] the Darkness, it was defeated by five greatnesses.
The first greatness is the Father of Greatness who exists in calm and hiddenness; as he is established in his light-earth, in his own essence.
Four greatnesses were manifested and came forth of him. They were appointed to ten parts, and established in total twelve.

The second greatness poured out and was manifested. It was revealed from the first greatness. It is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, together with the First Man and his five sons; these are the second greatness.
The third greatness is the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder, the Living Spirit, and the five sons of the Living Spirit. These are the third greatness.
The fourth greatness is the Third Ambassador, and the Pillar of Glory, and all the light powers who were revealed from him. These are the fourth greatness.
The fifth greatness who came from the Father is Jesus the Splendour, and all his powers whom he summoned, his emanations who were [established] They poured out and were manifested from him.

This is, so that they were spread out and [established in] fives: these five [sons] of the First Man [who support] the entire building; another five are the five sons of the Living Spirit who are spread out to five places, supporting [heaven and earth]

[These are a] total in twelve parts that [comprise the entire building. There are] another two added to them who are the summons and the obedience. They are the father and the mother whom Jesus the Splendour by his advent has appointed as successors to his place [in] the great earth and the [life] in them.

[The advent also] of the First Man who came [forth] belonging to [a king] existing in a kingdom [of great] esteem before they who belong to his household [But] his enemies [did him violence] and suffering by their wickedness; and they take from him [a glory] and a richness; and they imprison [him in] captivity and take from him their companies (?). Yet, he [overcomes] by his humility; and he takes heart and restrains his enemy [and endures] in silence.
Just as with this man, this noble son whose enemies surround him, this also is how the advent of the First Man happened, [against the] rulers, the enemies of the light.

In contrast, the advent of the Living Spirit and the commandment that he received, whereby he came upon all the rulers, it differs from that of the First Man. His advent [is greater than] the advent of the First Man.

The advent of the Living Spirit is like this, when he was sent from the greatness that he might bring up the First Man. He resembles a judge the king would send to overturn the violence to that man, the noble son against whom his enemies sinned. And he, this judge, [shall be] hard and cruel [against them] and he gives the means [to the noble son] by his righteousness and his strength; and he also judges all who are condemned according to their rebellious heart, and repays each according to his deserts. They who are worthy of blows he strikes with hard leather whips. Again, these who are worthy of cutting off their limbs, or indeed their [heads] and he repays them accordingly. [Others] and he binds and fetters them, and hangs by [their feet] and thus he does to them with a righteous judgement. And he kills them to flay their skin [from off them] so that they will be killed by a death [of great suffering] until they die. Again, [they for] whom it is fitting [and right] to banish from their dwellings he may remove according to a righteous judgement; just as they had faulted and sinned against the noble son.
Also, the associates in the mystery and the assistants of this judge, these who belong to him in great strength; in an instant and haste they shall do the will of their master.

Now, just as this genuine judge, who was sent from the king to overturn the violence to this man, the noble son: this is also the case with the Living Spirit. He also was sent from the King of the lights to overturn the vengeance and violence to the First Man, against whom the King of the realms of Darkness had sinned. He faulted and sinned against him, and also his rebellious powers. Therefore, when (the Living Spirit) came, he bore up the First Man.

Also, all the rulers, the powers of Sin who had faulted and sinned against the sons of the First Man, he has judged them according to a righteous judgement. He has bound them in heaven and earth. He put each one to the place fitting for him; he weighed each of them according to his cruelty and oppression. While some of them he enclosed in the prison, others he hung head down. Some [of them] are crucified, others are sat down all the time. Some among them are fixed beneath their associates, restricted by a strong chain; others he made the holders of authority over their companions beneath, so that they may do their pleasure amongst these below them.

[Know] that when the Father of Life established the judgements [upon them] He was revealed to all the powers of Darkness. He judged them as a true giver of judgement [in righteousness] This is the first judgement that the Living Spirit gave the rulers [in respect of the] First Man. Indeed, he gave victory to the First Man corresponding to his victory; but he condemned the King of the realms of Darkness corresponding to that by which he had erred.

[And] this chain, of this sort, became [the bond of] the earth till the end time when the universe will be dissolved; and it perishes in the great fire and is separated. While the light goes to its country, the Darkness remains in the chain and fetter for ever.

The advent also of the Third Ambassador, when he came to inspect they who are imprisoned in the zone: he is like a great king who comes and inspects craftsmen [and architects] and [artisans] and [all their works]

Also, they who are good, of the craftsmen and architects and artisans whom he has there in each place: he shall see that they have worked well, and have fallen to his works in their fashion. He shall rejoice with great joy [over them] He shall thank the artisans who have constructed his works [and completed] his orders.

Now, just as this great king who comes and inspects his works and fortifications, so also is the advent of the Third Ambassador. For, when he too came, he saw [his works] established and prepared and [the whole] series of the rulers prepared and established there, above and below, outside and within, in the great pattern that his brothers had made. They had come before him to the contest, they who had fixed and created the universe before he came. He saw the gods and the angels established and controlling the fortifications [and] guarding the entire ruling-power [of all things] which his first powers had done. They are the First Man and the Living Spirit and the Great Spirit, the Mother of Life.

Therefore, when he saw them, that they had created everything with great wisdom, [he rejoiced] as they looked he plundered (?) [the light] in his advent, by which he came, he was unveiled to them. He says to the Living Spirit: “The judgement that you have [given is] good, what you uttered [is righteous] you gave to them correspondingly; so that they were moved and raised up to that of which they were not worthy”.

Then the summons and the obedience, the great counsel that came to the elements, which are set in conjunction: it mixed with them, it was established in silence. It bears up [the light] until the end time when it can arise and stand firm in the great fire. It will gather to it its own soul, and sculpt it in the Last Statue. You will also find it sweeps out and casts from it the pollution that is foreign to it. However, the life and the light that are in all things it gathers in to it, and builds upon its body.

The time when this Last Statue will be perfect in all its limbs, then it can become free and ascend from that great struggle through the Living Spirit its father, the one who comes and brings a [living] limb. He brings it up from within this gathering (?), the melting down and destruction of all things.

Now, this counsel, that summons and obedience, resembles thus cooled butter. If a person will take and set it in hot milk, it melts down and soaks in with this hot milk. It melts in another time in silence and quiet to the midst [of the milk] yet also, of the power and the taste of this milk [all] is drawn to (the butter), and (the milk) sets and becomes cold [and still] in [its place] and the [impurity of] this milk it shall clarify and discard. However, the oil and the grease and the ‘beauty’ of the milk it shall gather in to it.

Again, this too is what the advent of that thought is like, the counsel of life, which is the summons and obedience that came to the elements. This is the one that at the end can arise and stand firm, and will gather in to it all the lives, and the light that has remained behind in everything. It can build them upon its body; it will gather them in to it [and sculpt them] in its image for ever and ever [beginning] from this time.

fills.explanation: Kephalaia chapters typically open with a topic-introducing formula, and 'Concerning the Darkness' introduces the subject of the chapter — how the Darkness was overcome.
The spiritual reading says 'brought into distinct existence,' and 'established' captures the emanations being constituted in their own being before they 'poured out and were manifested.'

The spiritual reading says 'arranged in complete orders,' and 'established in fives' parallels ¶3's 'established in total twelve,' using the chapter's consistent language for setting things into ordered groups.

The editor's 'sons' is confirmed: 'five sons of the First Man' is the standard Manichaean formula used consistently throughout the chapter (¶4, ¶8, ¶16); the spiritual reading's 'truths belonging to' is the correspondential translation of 'sons.'

The spiritual reading says 'constitute the entire spiritual structure,' and 'who support the entire building' parallels 'supporting' in the next clause about the Living Spirit's five sons, creating structural parallelism.

The five sons of the Living Spirit in Manichaean cosmology support the physical cosmos; the spiritual reading says 'the whole of spiritual order,' which in the Kephalaia's natural register corresponds to 'heaven and earth.'

The spiritual reading says 'In their fullness they form twelve orders,' and 'These are a total in twelve parts' is the natural summary statement connecting the two groups of five to the twelve total mentioned in ¶3.

fills.explanation: The twelve parts comprise the cosmic structure (the 'building' referenced in ¶8), and 'There are another two added' explains how the ten become twelve, matching ¶3's 'appointed to ten parts, and established in total twelve.'
The spiritual reading says 'within the ground of the church,' and 'in the great earth' naturally connects the summons and obedience's appointed place to the cosmic earth below.
The spiritual reading explicitly says 'life within them,' and 'the great earth and the life in them' pairs the ground of the church with the living principle dwelling within it.
Following the chapter's formulaic pattern for introducing each advent (¶19: 'The advent also of the Third Ambassador'), the First Man's advent is introduced with the same construction.
The Manichaean First Man 'came forth' from the Kingdom of Light to battle; 'came forth' is standard Kephalaia language for divine emanation or sending into combat.
The parable describes a noble son belonging to a king, consistent with ¶13 and ¶15 where 'the king' sends a judge; the noble son belongs to the royal household.
The spiritual reading says 'held in high regard,' and 'kingdom of great esteem' naturally describes the noble son's honored position before his household.
The spiritual reading indicates a contrast ('yet its enemies'), and 'But' provides the necessary contrastive conjunction between the noble son's honored position and his enemies' attack.
The spiritual reading says 'assaulted it and inflicted suffering,' and 'did him violence' connects directly to the repeated phrase 'overturn the violence to that man' used in ¶13 and ¶15.

The spiritual reading says 'its truths and its spiritual abundance'; in the Kephalaia, the First Man's light-armour taken by darkness corresponds to 'a glory,' which parallels 'and a richness' in structure.
The editor's 'him in' is confirmed: in the parable, the noble son is imprisoned by his enemies, and 'they imprison him in captivity' is natural narrative syntax.
The spiritual reading says 'prevails by its own self-emptying humility,' and 'overcomes by his humility' describes the noble son's paradoxical victory through patient endurance.
The spiritual reading emphasizes 'patient silence,' and 'restrains his enemy and endures in silence' completes a tricolon of passive resistance: takes heart, restrains, endures.
The spiritual reading says 'against the dominant falsities,' and 'against the rulers' specifies that the First Man's advent was directed in combat opposition to the archons of Darkness.

The spiritual reading says the Living Spirit's advent 'follows upon and completes' the first combat; since the text already stated it 'differs,' this sentence specifies the qualitative superiority of the judicial advent.
The spiritual reading says 'is severe and unyielding,' and 'this judge shall be hard and cruel' introduces the judge's character using the Kephalaia's prophetic-teaching register.
The judge is described as hard and cruel 'against them' — the enemies of the noble son — before turning to describe how he gives means of deliverance to the victim.
The judge provides means of restoration to the victim; 'he gives the means to the noble son by his righteousness' specifies the recipient, consistent with the parable's narrative of rescue.

The spiritual reading says 'their very capacity to act'; in the escalating punishments (blows → cutting limbs → cutting heads), 'heads' represents the ultimate deprivation of capacity, corresponding to decapitation.

The passage follows a pattern of categorizing punishments ('They who are worthy of blows... these who are worthy of cutting off...'); 'Others' introduces the next category of offenders who are bound and fettered.
The spiritual reading says 'inversion of their own state,' and hanging by the feet inverts the person head-downward — directly paralleling ¶16's 'others he hung head down.'
The spiritual reading says 'stripping their outermost covering,' and 'flay their skin from off them' completes the action of flaying — removing the outer covering entirely.
The phrase 'until they die' implies a prolonged, lingering death; 'a death of great suffering' fits the escalating judicial punishments and the passage's emphasis on proportional retribution.
The editor's 'they for' is confirmed: 'they for whom it is fitting to banish' is a standard relative construction introducing the final category of punished offenders.
The doubling 'fitting and right' is characteristic of the legal-judicial register of this passage, reinforcing the legitimacy of banishment as a righteous judgment.
Following the pattern in ¶16 ('some of them he enclosed... others he hung...'), 'some of them are crucified' continues the categorization of punished rulers.

Kephalaia didactic discourse regularly opens new teaching sections with imperative 'Know' (or 'Understand'), and 'Know that when the Father of Life established the judgements' introduces the theological summary of the Living Spirit's judgment.
The judgements were established 'upon' the powers of Darkness; 'established the judgements upon them' specifies the recipients of judgment before describing its public revelation.

The chapter repeatedly emphasizes 'righteous judgement' (¶13, ¶16, ¶31); 'a true giver of judgement in righteousness' completes the characterization before the summary statement 'This is the first judgement.'
The editor's 'in respect of the' is confirmed: the judgment was given to the rulers on account of their sin against the First Man, and 'in respect of' captures this causal/relational sense.
The conjunction 'And' continues the narrative from the judgment described in ¶17 to its cosmological consequence — the lasting chain binding the earth until the end time.

The spiritual reading says 'the fixed order of the external church'; the chain 'became the bond of the earth' means the judicial binding became the lasting restraining order holding the cosmos until dissolution.
Paragraph 20 lists 'craftsmen and architects and artisans'; the parable in ¶19 introduces the same categories, and 'architects' is the second type of worker the king inspects.
Following the list in ¶20 ('craftsmen and architects and artisans'), 'artisans' is the third type of skilled worker in the parable of the king's inspection.
Paragraph 21 says the king 'inspects his works and fortifications'; beyond the three worker types, the king also inspects 'all their works,' bridging to the structures described in the application.

The king rejoices 'over them' — over the workers and their good labour — before then thanking the artisans individually, following the natural progression from general delight to specific acknowledgment.
The editor's 'and completed' is confirmed: 'constructed his works and completed his orders' pairs building with finishing, and matches the spiritual reading's 'and fulfilled.'
The editor's 'his works' is confirmed: 'he saw his works established and prepared' directly parallels ¶20's description and matches the spiritual reading's 'the spiritual structures.'
The spiritual reading says 'the orderings of all states arranged'; 'the whole series of the rulers prepared and established there' describes the complete cosmic ordering the Ambassador surveyed.
A simple conjunction connecting two parallel participial actions: 'controlling the fortifications and guarding the entire ruling-power.'

The spiritual reading says 'the entire governance of divine order which the primary emanations accomplished'; 'the ruling-power of all things' specifies the universal scope of what the first powers established.

Paralleling ¶20 where the king 'shall rejoice with great joy' upon seeing the good work, the Ambassador likewise rejoices upon seeing everything created with great wisdom — the application mirrors the parable.

The Third Ambassador's central function in the Kephalaia is the liberation of captive light from the cosmic zone; the spiritual reading confirms 'it liberated,' and 'the light' is the characteristic object of the Ambassador's redemptive work.

The spiritual reading says 'established is good'; in the judicial register of the chapter, 'The judgement that you have given is good' is the Ambassador's commendation to the Living Spirit for his righteous verdict.

The chapter repeatedly emphasizes righteous judgement; 'what you uttered is righteous, you gave to them correspondingly' affirms that the Living Spirit's decree was just before noting its proportional execution.

The summons and obedience bear up 'the light' — the captive light particles dispersed in the elements — until the end time when they can be gathered into the Last Statue, matching the Manichaean soteriology of light-gathering.

The spiritual reading says 'restored faculty'; in the Kephalaia, 'living' is the natural-register term for what has been redeemed and animated by divine light, and 'a living limb' describes each rescued part of the Last Statue.

The butter melts 'to the midst of the milk' — completing the spatial description of butter dissolving into the center of the hot milk, which is the only grammatically and contextually possible complement.

The spiritual reading indicates that the essential quality of the natural truth is entirely drawn toward celestial good; 'all is drawn to the butter' clarifies that every good element of the milk is attracted to the butter.

The spiritual reading says 'becomes still'; the milk becomes 'cold and still' once the good part (butter) has been extracted, matching the analogy's earlier vocabulary of 'silence and quiet' for the passive state.
After the essential good has been drawn out, the milk settles 'in its place' — remaining in its own inert state — before the butter clarifies and discards the impurity from it.

The spiritual reading says 'the merely natural and external'; in the butter analogy, 'the impurity of this milk' is what gets clarified and discarded, connecting to ¶26's 'pollution that is foreign to it.'

The spiritual reading says 'in the likeness of the Divine'; 'gather them in and sculpt them in its image' directly parallels ¶26's 'sculpt it in the Last Statue,' using the chapter's own language of spiritual formation.

The word 'beginning' naturally bridges the eternal formula and the temporal marker, creating the closing declaration 'for ever and ever, beginning from this time' — specifying the point from which the eternal gathering into the Divine image commences.
